headline: Linux Leaves RTX Spark Running on Empty
lede: On native Linux, Nvidia’s RTX Spark laptop delivers just a fraction of its plugged-in inference speed. An encrypted Windows-only power-management table holds the GPU near 780 MHz, while WSL approaches Windows performance.

headline: Kitty 0.50 Restores the Terminal Session
lede: Release 0.50 adds docked windows, persistent sessions, workspace-style tabs, and richer graphics controls. The terminal grows into a programmable desktop workspace: fast, stateful, and still sharply configurable.

headline: Verified Answers Still Need Human Judgment
lede: AI can produce and check a proof without making its meaning legible to science. Jessica Hullman argues that knowledge also requires interpretation, accountability, criticism, and people able to decide which results matter.
pullquote: A correct answer is not yet scientific knowledge.

headline: GitHub Stumbles Across the Development Stack
lede: Git operations, Issues, Pull Requests, APIs, and Actions all suffered elevated errors and intermittent failure. GitHub applied mitigations, but the incident again asks how much of a team’s workflow should depend on one forge.

headline: A Browser Sheet Bends Like Jelly
lede: Drag the surface, pause the simulation, and watch a digital sheet fold through space. This compact Codevember experiment turns browser graphics and cloth physics into a small, tactile curiosity.

headline: Gemini’s Paid Chats Still Feed the Machine
lede: A personal Gemini account may send saved conversations into Google’s service-improvement and training processes, even behind a paid subscription. Keeping history on preserves convenience; turning it off limits retention but changes the bargain.

headline: A Car Clock Yields to the Jailbreak
lede: A 2014 Renault made changing the time depend on a licensed navigation card. Reverse-engineering its Linux-based unit, the author combined a path traversal with crash-handler execution to reclaim a simple setting from proprietary software.

headline: Stringman Puts a Room-Scale Robot on Cables
lede: Four ceiling-mounted motors suspend an open-source gripper across a workspace, with printed parts, software, datasets, and APIs released for builders. The $800 design favors reach and coverage over payload, dexterity, and easy household installation.

headline: Before Malloc, Memory Had a Map
lede: Recovered Unix sources show early allocators working directly against core and swap maps, using first-fit placement, coalescing, and rollback. Their arena-oriented design offers an old answer to modern questions about ownership, isolation, and lifetime.

headline: Hinton Warns Against an Unchecked AI Race
lede: Geoffrey Hinton sees possible gains from AI, but also risks to power grids, financial infrastructure, and public trust. He calls for independent testing, mandatory evaluations, and international standards before competition outruns restraint.
